newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Long Australian bonds get boost from U.S.
newsitem.headline: Long Australian bonds get boost from U.S.

text.p: *Long Australian bonds got off to a strong start to the week, triggered by Friday's rally in U.S. Treasuries.
*TCV to hold bond tender at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
Long Australian bonds got off to a strong start to the week, triggered by Friday's rally in U.S. Treasuries and continuing the recent short end-led advance.
Foreign buying and hopes of continued moderating growth sent the U.S. market higher on Friday, and an already bullish local market needed little excuse to follow the trend.

Speculation of a possible further easing in monetary policy following a surprisingly weak retail trade report on Friday took three-year bond yields to their lowest level since February 1994 on Friday, and June and September bill futures go to a discount to 5.5 percent official cash rates.

The bid tone is likely to be maintained going into Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting with the market leaving nothing to chance after being caught totally off-guard with the central bank cut rate just over a week ago.

The market will get another indication of current demand with the release of April building approvals at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). After four falls in the last five months economists are forecasting a 3.0 percent rise, according to a Reuters survey.
Before then Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) is due to hold an A$100 million bond tender at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT). Details of the tender are due at 10.00 a.m. (2400 GMT).

The local short end gave up some ground to U.S. and Canada after last week's strong outperformance. However, the long end outperformed Canada, which holds its general election today. New Zealand markets were closed for the Queen's Birthday holiday.
